This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run** example that shows how to launch a new Compute Engine VM in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) that:

| Requirement | How we satisfy it |
|-------------|-------------------|
| **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS** | `--image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts` + `--image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud` |
| **RTX A6000 GPU** | `--accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| **Sufficient CPU & RAM** | `--machine-type=e2-standard-8` (adjust as needed) |
| **Boot disk size** | `--boot-disk-size=100GB` (you can change the size) |
| **Public IP** | `--no-address` (omit if you want one) |
| **Firewall rules** | `--tags=http-server,https-server` (opens ports 80 & 443) |

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a GCP project with billing enabled.  
> * The Compute Engine API must be enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You need the `gcloud` SDK installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  

---

## 1️⃣ Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="e2-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM (change if you need more)
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
    --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="pd-balanced" \
    --accelerator="count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000" \
    --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \        # Optional: set what happens during maintenance
    --restart-on-failure \
    --network-interface="network-tier=PREMIUM,subnet=default" \
    --tags="http-server,https-server" \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # Optional: run a script at boot
    --no-address \                               # Omit if you want a public IP
    --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
    --service-account="default" \
    --labels="env=demo,gpu=true"
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | Defines CPU/RAM. `e2-standard-8` gives 8 vCPU + 32 GiB RAM. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Sets the root disk size/type. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the NVIDIA Tesla A6000 GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Controls behavior during host maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts the VM if it crashes. |
| `--network-interface` | Uses the default subnet in the selected zone. |
| `--tags` | Opens firewall ports 80 & 443. |
| `--metadata-from-file` | Runs a custom shell script at first boot (optional). |
| `--no-address` | Prevents allocation of a public IP (useful for private VMs). |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access. |
| `--service-account` | Uses the default service account (or specify another). |
| `--labels` | Adds key/value metadata for filtering/tagging. |

---

## 2️⃣ Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to use the raw REST endpoint, here’s a minimal JSON payload you can POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/e2-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      },
      "autoDelete": true,
      "type": "PERSISTENT"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": []  // Empty array → no external IP
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "labels": {
    "env": "demo",
    "gpu": "true"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Endpoint

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
```

Replace `{project}` and `{zone}` with your actual project ID and zone.

### Authentication

Use OAuth 2.0 with a scope of `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute`. The easiest way is via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick One‑liner (for scripts)

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
    --zone=us-central1-a \
    --machine-type=e2-standard-8 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000 \
    --no-address \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh
```

> **Tip:** Save the above command into a shell script (`create_gpu_instance.sh`) and make it executable (`chmod +x create_gpu_instance.sh`). Then run `./create_gpu_instance.sh`.

---

## 4️⃣ After Creation

Once the instance is running:

1. SSH into it:
   ```bash
   gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --zone=us-central1-a
   ```
2. Verify GPU visibility:
   ```bash
   nvidia-smi
   ```
3. Install CUDA Toolkit (if needed):
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-1
   ```

---

### Summary

* **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ...` – quickest for interactive use.  
* **REST**: JSON payload – great for programmatic automation or Terraform/Pulumi integration.  
* **GPU**: `nvidia-tesla-a6000` – the RTX A6000 is available in GCP under the “NVIDIA Tesla” family.  

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or add additional scopes/metadata as per your workload requirements. Happy GPU computing!
